items.response: That fits the symptom: Stripe signs the exact raw bytes, and Fastify's default JSON parser hands the route a re-serialised object, so the signature never matches. I'll register fastify-raw-body for the /v1/webhooks/stripe route only and pass the raw payload to the Stripe signature check. Action: find where the api registers plugins and the Stripe webhook handler, add fastify-raw-body scoped to that route, and test it with app.inject() using a signed payload.

The signing secret must never be in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable, since those get exposed to the browser. So share-link.ts will use a server-only env var and `import 'server-only'`, which also avoids the node:crypto 'Can't resolve fs' style build error if it leaks into a client component. The preview button is a client component, so it will call a server action (or small route) that returns the signed link. Action: write apps/web/lib/share-link.ts with an HMAC over invoice id + expiry, add the server action, wire the copy button in the preview component, and add the new secret to .env.example as a placeholder.
